title: Berlin Market Halls - FAQ
subtitle: Which old halls still work, when to go and what happened to the rest.

items.q: How many market halls does Berlin have?
items.a: Berlin opened **14 municipal market halls** between 1886 and 1892. **Four** still sell food today: Markthalle Neun, the Arminiusmarkthalle, the Marheineke Markthalle and the Ackerhalle, which houses a supermarket.

items.q: Are Berlin's market halls open on Sundays?
items.a: No. All four are **closed on Sundays and public holidays**. Markthalle Neun sometimes holds a special market on a Sunday, so check its calendar. Otherwise a flea market or a weekly market is the better Sunday plan.

items.q: When is Street Food Thursday at Markthalle Neun?
items.a: Every **Thursday from 17:00 to 22:00** (checked on 11 November 2026). Arrive around 17:30 if you want to eat before the queues build after 19:00.

items.q: What are the opening hours of the Arminiusmarkthalle?
items.a: The hall is open **Monday to Saturday, 8:00 to 22:00**. Food stalls sell from about 10:00 to 20:00 (18:00 on Saturday), and the kitchens and bars run from **12:00 to 22:00**. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays.

items.q: What happened to the Central Market Hall at Alexanderplatz?
items.a: It opened in **1886** with its own rail siding off the Stadtbahn, was badly bombed in 1944 and was later demolished. The widened Stadtbahn viaduct that once fed it is the main trace left.

items.q: Which Berlin market hall is the most original?
items.a: From the outside, the **Ackerhalle** in Mitte: it is the only hall whose exterior is still in its original 1888 state. Inside it is a supermarket. For the old atmosphere with stalls, the **Arminiusmarkthalle** in Moabit has kept its iron frame and has been in use since 1891.
